The Court made the following ORDER:
 The instant criminal petition under Section 482 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 (in short, "Cr.P.C.") has been filed by the Petitioners/A1 to A5 in C.C.No.1230 of 2018 on the file of I Additional Chief Metropolitan Magistrate, Visakhapatnam seeking quashment of the case for the offences punishable under Sections 498-A, 323 IPC.
 2  VJP,J  CRLP.No.2775/2022 2.

Heard Sri Sreemannarayana Vattikuti, learned counsel for the Busi Ratna Kumari vs The State Of Andhra Pradesh on 6 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/175783291/
1 petitioners and Ms., learned Assistant Public Prosecutor for the respondent No.1.

sentences.text: The notice is served on the respondent No.2 but they did not turn up.

3. The petitioners herein are A1 to A5 who are mother in law, sister in law,
her husband, another sister in law and her husband respectively to the de-facto complainant/respondent No.2 herein.

4. Learned counsel for the petitioners would submit that after the death of the husband of the respondent No.2, this case has been lodged against the family members of the husband only to harass them.
Learned counsel further would submit that the husband of the respondent No.2 died on 20.12.2015.

Thereafter, respondent No.2 filed a civil suit in O.S.No.345 of 2017 on the file of II Additional Senior Civil Judge, Visakhapatnam wherein I.A.No.270 of 2017 has been filed for temporary injunction which dismissed on merits on 29.08.2017.

entities.text: II Additional Senior Civil Judge, Visakhapatnam
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Later, the present case has been lodged against the petitioners on 05.02.2018.
Learned counsel for the petitioners further would submit that the petitioner Nos. 3 and 5/A4 and A5 are residents of gulf countries due to their employment.

Learned counsel further would submit that by making all false averments, the civil suit has been filed seeking partition relating to a property which was purchased by the husband of the A1 by way of Registered Sale deed even in the year 1983.

The names of husband of A1 and husband of the respondent No.2 appear to be similar, taking advantage of the same,
the respondent No.2 filed the civil suit only to grab the said property.
Learned  3  VJP,J  CRLP.No.2775/2022 counsel for the petitioners further would submit that Accused No.1 is aged about 75 years.

Learned counsel finally would submit that even as per the contents of the complaint, no offence has been made out prima facie against Busi Ratna Kumari vs The State Of Andhra Pradesh on 6 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/175783291/
2 the petitioners, then continuing the criminal proceedings against the petitioners is sheer abuse of process of law.
5.

sentences.text: Learned Assistant Public Prosecutor opposed the petition and would submit that there are allegations made against the petitioners in the complaint as well as in the charge sheet and court may pass appropriate orders.

6. A bare perusal of Section 482 makes it clear that the Code envisages that inherent powers of the High Court are not limited or affected so as to make orders as may be necessary; (i) to give effect to any order under the Code or, (ii) to prevent abuse of the process of any Court or, otherwise (iii) to secure ends of justice.
A court while sitting in Section 482 jurisdiction is not functioning as a trial court, court of appeal or a court of revision.
It must exercise its powers to do real and substantial justice, depending on the facts and circumstances of the case.
These powers must be invoked for compelling reasons of abuse of process of law or glaring injustice, which are against sound principles of criminal jurisprudence.

7. In Kahkashan Kausar @ Sonam vs. State of Bihar case1,it was held by the Hon'ble Apex Court as follows:
1  2022 1 S.C.R 558  4  VJP,J  CRLP.No.2775/2022  "18. The above-mentioned decisions clearly demonstrate

entities.text: Kahkashan Kausar @ Sonam vs. State of Bihar
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: that  this court has at numerous instances expressed concern over  the misuse of section 498A IPC and the increased tendency  of implicating relatives of the husband in matrimonial  disputes, without analysing the long term ramifications of a  trial on the complainant as well as the accused.

It is further  manifest from the said judgments that false implication by  way of general omnibus allegations made in the course of Busi Ratna Kumari vs The State Of Andhra Pradesh on 6 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/175783291/
3  matrimonial dispute, if left unchecked would result in misuse  of the process of law.

entities.text: Busi Ratna Kumari vs The State Of Andhra Pradesh on 6 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Therefore, this court by way of its  judgments has warned the courts from proceeding against  the relatives and in-laws of the husband when no prima facie  case is made out against them.
 ****
22.Therefore

, upon consideration of the relevant circumstances and in the absence of any specific role attributed to the accused appellants, it would be unjust if the Appellants are forced to go through the tribulations of a trial, i.e., general and omnibus allegations cannot manifest in a situation where the relatives of the complainant's husband are forced to undergo trial.

It has been highlighted by this court in varied instances, that a criminal trial leading to an eventual acquittal also inflicts severe scars upon the accused, and such an exercise must therefore be discouraged."
(emphasis supplied)
8.
Considering the submissions made and a fair look at the contents of the complaint would reveal that the marriage of the respondent No.2 and son of A1 took place on 19.07.2007.
As can be seen from the complaint, the husband of Accused No.1 died on 24.12.2012.
Till then, no allegations were made by the petitioners by the respondent No.2.
It is her contention that after the death of her father-in-law and further after the death of her husband i.e., VJP,J on 20.12.2015, the petitioners started harassing her.

The complaint further would show that the husband of the respondent No.2 left for Ethiopia due to employment, thereafter disputes arose between respondent No.2 and her husband due to which he returned to India.

A stray question has been referred in the complaint dated 20.12.2016, according to her, she was beaten by the petitioners and joined in K.G Hospital,
Visakhapatnam.

As can be seen from the record, the present case has been lodged on 05.08.2018,
had it been true, she would have lodged the complaint immediately thereafter.

Admittedly, she has filed the civil suit which pending before the civil court wherein her petition for temporary injunction was dismissed on merits on 29.08.2017 as rightly put by learned counsel for the petitioners.
Except making omnibus allegations against the petitioners, no specific extent has been referred against the petitioners in the complaint.
All the allegations made are vague.
Therefore.
this court is of the considered opinion that continuing criminal proceedings against the petitioners is mere abuse of process of law.
9. In the result, the Criminal Petition is allowed.
The criminal proceedings against the petitioners in C.C.No.1230 of 2018 on the file of I Additional Chief Metropolitan Magistrate, Visakhapatnam are hereby quashed.
